newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta to go on strengthening versus mark - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Peseta to go on strengthening versus mark - Salomon.

text.p: The recent peseta strengthening against the mark will probably persist in coming months, Salomon Brothers wrote in its weekly report on Monday.
The external surplus and above-trend economic growth favour a stronger Spanish unit versus the mark, it said.

The Bank of Spain appears to favour a range of 84 to 85 pesetas per mark for now and probably expects the peseta to join the euro at the current ERM central parity of 85.07 pesetas per mark, the weekly bank report said.

"However the existing short-term interest rate differential versus Germany justifies a level closer to 83 pesetas where the forward exchange rate at January 1999 would coincide with present ERM central parity," he said.

At 1230 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.28/30 per mark versus 84.28/30 at the close on Friday. During the past week the mark hit a record low at 84.13 and then bounced back on dealer talk of Bank of Spain intervention.
But Salomon added that despite peseta strength, the Bank of Spain is unlikely to cut its 5.25-percent official rate any time soon.
"With economic growth already above trend and inflation gradually turning up, the Bank of Spain is unlikely to lower short-term interest rates any time soon," the report said.
But economic fundamentals suggest the peseta could climb to further gains, Salomon added.
"The recent external performance of the Spanish economy suggests that the peseta is moderately undervalued on a competitive basis," it said.

"..different measures suggest that the real trade-weighted peseta probably is about five percent lower than its long-term trend. This trend shows a 1/2 percent annual increase during the past 35 years, probably reflecting faster productivity gains in the tradable sector than among Spain's trading partners".
